title: Accelerate and Deepen Efforts Against Climate Change
what_it_is: Accelerate and Deepen Efforts Against Climate Change

sections.label: Wettest January in 100 years
sections.summary: The past January was the wettest January in the past 100 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The past January was the wettest January in the past 100 years.

sections.label: Hottest decades and Singapore heating
sections.summary: The past two decades were the hottest on record, and Singapore is becoming hotter twice as quickly as the rest of the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The past two decades were also the hottest decades on record.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But if you think you are sweaty now, get ready to sweat more: Singapore is becoming hotter twice as quickly as the rest of the world.

sections.label: Taxpayer spending on polders
sections.summary: Tens of billions of taxpayer dollars will have to be spent on massive projects such as building polders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Tens of billions of taxpayer dollars will have to be spent on massive projects, such as building polders.

sections.label: Melting ice caps and shipping routes
sections.summary: The polar ice caps will melt, opening new shipping routes that bypass Singapore's port.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The polar ice caps will melt, opening new shipping routes that bypass Singapore’s port.

sections.label: Government contracts and procurement sustainability
sections.summary: In 2016, 35,000 Government contracts were worth $22.6 billion, and the Government can move industries' practices by enhancing its sustainability standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In 2016, our 35,000 Government contracts were worth a whopping $22.6 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As the largest employer and one of the biggest business clients in Singapore, the Government can move the standard business practices of entire industries, just by enhancing its sustainability standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is good that we have the Public Service Taking The Lead in Environmental Sustainability initiative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is also good news that Minister Grace Fu said last year that the Government is already looking at a sustainable framework for Government procurement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, life-cycle costing should be expanded to more categories of products.

sections.label: Life-cycle costing for more products
sections.summary: The Government requires life-cycle costing only for electrical appliances, and it should also be done for vehicles, furniture and other products.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Government currently requires its agencies to do it only for electrical appliances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We should do it also for vehicles, furniture and other products.

sections.label: Air-conditioner efficiency tick standards
sections.summary: Public procurement standards require air-conditioners to have three ticks of efficiency, and the standard can be raised to four or five ticks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For example, public procurement standards currently require air-conditioners to have only three ticks of efficiency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We can raise the standard to four or five ticks, which will save us money in the long run while cutting emissions.

sections.label: Singapore land carbon emissions
sections.summary: Because much forest has been cut down in recent years, Singapore's land now emits more carbon than it absorbs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In fact, because we have cut down so much forest in recent years, Singapore's land now emits more carbon than it absorbs.

sections.label: Penalties for non-compliant developers
sections.summary: Developers must comply or they may be punished by $50,000 fines or six months' imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Developers must comply, or they may be punished by $50,000 fines or six months' imprisonment.

sections.label: Carbon tax revenue for industry efficiency
sections.summary: The Government is spending more than $1 billion in carbon tax revenue over the next five years to help industries become more efficient.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Government is listening and has done a great deal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We are spending more than $1 billion in carbon tax revenue for the next five years to help our industries become more efficient.

sections.label: 2050 net zero emissions target
sections.summary: The passage calls for committing to 2050 as a target year for net zero emissions to catch up to countries such as Korea and Japan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Let us commit to 2050 as a target year for net zero emissions so we catch up to the many countries we often compare ourselves to, such as Korea and Japan.

sections.label: Transboundary Haze Pollution Act 2014
sections.summary: In 2014, during the peak haze period, the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act was passed to prosecute companies engaged in illegal forest burning causing severe air pollution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In 2014, during the peak of the haze period, we passed the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act that allowed regulators to prosecute local and foreign companies that engaged in illegal forest burning that causes severe air pollution.

sections.label: Dover Forest feedback deadline extended
sections.summary: After residents raised concerns about losing Dover Forest to BTO flats, the Minister extended public feedback on the Environmental Based Study by four weeks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I might note that when the news that Dover Forest might be developed to build BTO flats, I received many emails, dozens and dozens of emails and Facebook messages and WhatsApp and in conversations, person to person conversation at Meet-the-People Session, from residents expressing their concern at the loss of the forest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: So, following my discussion with MND, I am very happy that Minister Desmond Lee has extended the deadline for public feedback to the Environmental Based Study by a full four weeks.

sections.label: Ulu Pandan nature trail aspiration
sections.summary: The speaker aspires to partner with NParks to build a nature trail from Holland Green Linear Park through Clementi Forest to Clementi Road.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: One aspiration I have for Ulu Pandan is to partner with NParks in building a nature trail from Holland Green Linear Park that will weave its wave through the contours of Clementi Forest all the way to Clementi Road.

sections.label: Climate action, composting and Paris Agreement
sections.summary: The passage covers food composting with NEA at Ghim Moh Market, Paris Agreement warming limits, IPCC warnings, and empowering stakeholders on climate change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Furthermore, in partnership with NEA, we can introduce food composting to the community and we plan to introduce that to Ghim Moh Market and Food Centre.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: At the global scale, when the Paris Agreement was adopted in 2015, nations around the world came together with the aim of limiting global warming to 1.5-degree Celsius above pre-industrial levels with an understanding that a two-degree Celsius rise would lead to major environmental risks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In 2019, the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) warned that: one, we have already reached warming of one-degree Celsius; two, that we are likely to reach 1.5-degree Celsius between 2030 and 2052; and three, that a slate of worrying impacts involving changes to sea level, temperature and rainfall will still be experienced by 2100 even if warming is limited to 1.5-degree Celsius.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Sea level rise, threats to our water and food security, and an increased risk of vector-borne diseases are but a few of these impacts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Addressing this challenge will require us to acknowledge the urgency of the threats before us and to empower multiple stakeholders – from businesses and the public, to civil society including academia and NGOs – to come together to respond to the threat of climate change.

sections.label: Singapore sea level rise risk
sections.summary: With 30% of land within 15 metres above mean sea level, sea level rise could inundate low-lying areas, possibly rising half a metre by 2100.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: With 30% of our land lying within 15 metres above mean sea level, sea level rise in the longer term could inundate low-lying areas including neighbourhoods, vital industrial areas and parts of the Central Business District.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Last year, I mentioned in the House that even under an optimistic emissions scenario, sea level in Singapore could rise by half a metre by 2100.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Studies also suggest that IPCC projections for global mean sea level rise by 2100 tend to be conservative, where high emissions scenarios are concerned.

sections.label: Amendment includes civil society
sections.summary: The purpose of the amendment is to include civil society in this call.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: The purpose of our amendment is to include civil society in this call.

sections.label: Singapore primary forest and vegetation cover
sections.summary: Primary forests cover about 0.28% of Singapore's area, and under 20.2% is covered by vegetation not dominated by human management.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Today, we live in an urban landscape where primary forests cover only approximately 0.28% of our area and where less than 20.2% is covered by vegetation that is not dominated by human management, although with varying degrees of protection under the law.

sections.label: Clementi Forest zoning status
sections.summary: The Government said Clementi Forest's residential zoning is retained, with future generations deciding on housing if needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: In response to my Parliamentary Question on the status of Clementi Forest in January this year, the Government claimed that the zoning of the site for residential use will be retained, while giving our future generations the option of deciding whether to use it for housing, if the need arises.

sections.label: Protecting secondary forests and amendments
sections.summary: It proposes more legal protection for secondary forests and inserts amendments on a climate emergency and civil society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Thirdly, provide more secondary forests with greater protection under the law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: A portion of these areas could be afforded greater protection, similar to those in nature reserves, while others could be regulated under the different regime to enable Singaporeans to benefit from simpler recreational activities which are less destructive in nature.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: If we fail to take bolder steps to safeguard our forested areas and if we fail to improve our land use planning in non-forested areas today, we will leave our future generation to the landscape deprived of enough areas to even consider conserving and perhaps more worryingly, we will leave them with the mindset that tomorrow's problems are for tomorrow's generations to solve.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: It has been proposed as amendments: "(1) In line 2, after the words, 'That this House', to insert the words 'acknowledges a climate emergency and'; and (2) In line 2 after the words, 'private sector', to insert a comma and the words 'civil society'." It may be convenient that the debate on the Original Motion and on any other amendments moved by Members be proceeded with simultaneously as a debate on a single question.

sections.label: Total Defence conceptualised in 1984
sections.summary: Singapore's Total Defence was conceptualised in 1984 to underscore a whole-of-society approach to national security.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Singapore's Total Defence was conceptualised in 1984 to underscore the importance of a whole-of-society approach to national security.

sections.label: Digital Defence as sixth pillar
sections.summary: Digital Defence was added as a sixth pillar, reflecting the need to handle online threats such as fake news.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Digital Defence was subsequently added as a sixth pillar, a move that rightly reflected the need for Singaporeans to be aware and better equipped to handle online threats to Singapore society such as fake news.

sections.label: Proposing a Climate Defence pillar
sections.summary: The Member asks the House to consider adding another pillar, Climate Defence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Today, I am asking this House to consider adding another pillar – Climate Defence.

sections.label: Climate change as high-risk threat
sections.summary: Climate change and effects like rising sea levels pose high-risk threats, and the Prime Minister said to treat climate defences like the SAF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Like other types of threats that Singapore face, climate change and its associated effects such as rising sea levels pose clear and high-risk threats towards the well-being of Singapore and Singaporeans, as well as our way of life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: This is seen in the 2019 National Day Rally where the Prime Minister, let me quote him – he said, "we should treat climate change defences like we treat the SAF – with utmost seriousness".

sections.label: Climate Defence as Total Defence pillar
sections.summary: Adopting Climate Defence as a Total Defence pillar shows Singapore is a responsible international community member that can be trusted to adhere to Paris Climate Agreement goals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: By adopting Climate Defence as a pillar of Total Defence, it demonstrates that Singapore is a responsible member of the international community with regards to climate change and can be trusted to adhere to the goals set under the Paris Climate Agreement.

sections.label: Call for Climate Defence pillar
sections.summary: The passage calls for new laws, regulations, market changes, will, attention and resources, and for Climate Defence to become the seventh Total Defence pillar.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Aside from behavioural nudges, there must be resolution towards new laws and regulations; there must be a new willingness to make the market work for the environment, there must be more will, more attention and more resources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The Government has already said that it is committed to working on the mitigation measures against climate change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Let us make Climate Defence the seventh pillar of our Total Defence.

sections.label: Embodied carbon in new construction
sections.summary: Embodied carbon will account for half the carbon footprint of new construction developments between now and 2050, consuming much of the remaining carbon budget.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Embodied carbon will be responsible for half of the entire carbon footprint of new construction developments between now and 2050, threatening to consume a large part of our remaining carbon budget.

sections.label: Green legislation and net zero buildings
sections.summary: Government and private businesses must implement green legislation and change industry standards, setting a 2050 goal of net zero operational carbon for new buildings, infrastructure and renovations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Government and private businesses have to look towards implementing rigorous green legislation and change industry standards and business processes, especially within the construction industry where new buildings must be designed to be more carbon efficient.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We should set our 2050 carbon emissions goal for all new buildings, infrastructure and renovations to be net zero operational carbon.

sections.label: Green Mark Scheme adoption
sections.summary: Over the last 16 years, the Green Mark Scheme has been widely adopted and more than 4,000 Singapore buildings have earned the BCA Green Mark award.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Over the last 16 years, the Green Mark Scheme has been widely adopted and more than 4,000 buildings in Singapore have earned the BCA Green Mark award.

sections.label: Green Mark embodied carbon scoring
sections.summary: The Green Mark Scheme includes carbon accounting but allocates only two of 100 points for embodied carbon, allowing buildings to score highly despite being concrete-intensive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Currently, the Green Mark Scheme includes carbon accounting.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: However, this scheme allocates only two out of 100 points for embodied carbon accounting.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The assessment allows buildings to score highly despite performing poorly on certain measures of carbon intensiveness, which actually means buildings can be certified as Green Mark Silver, Gold, Platinum or Zero Energy despite being extremely concrete-intensive.

sections.label: Green Mark demolition recycling point
sections.summary: Under the Green Mark Scheme, one point is awarded if 35% of demolished concrete is handled by a recycling contractor.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: When it comes to demolition work, under the Green Mark Scheme, one point is awarded if 35% of demolished concrete, is handled by a recycling contractor.

sections.label: Zero Energy Certification building
sections.summary: A building designed by NUS Design and Environment with partners is Southeast Asia's first to receive Zero Energy Certification from the International Living Future Institute.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: That was designed by NUS Design and Environment, in partnership with external consultants, developers and builders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It is the first building in Southeast Asia to be awarded the Zero Energy Certification by the International Living Future Institute, which is one of the world's most prestigious sustainability organisations.

sections.label: Circular financing scheme incentive
sections.summary: An incentive example is a circular financing scheme with grants to developers from a central pool of carbon taxes collected from the building industry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: An example of an incentive could be creating a circular financing scheme, by way of grants awarded to developers from a central pool of carbon taxes collected from within the building industry.

sections.label: Singapore updated NDC submission
sections.summary: In March 2020, Singapore submitted an updated Nationally Determined Contribution to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In March 2020, Singapore submitted an updated Nationally Determined Contribution to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).

sections.label: Updated NDC emissions targets
sections.summary: The updated NDC reiterates peaking emissions at 65 million tonnes around 2030 and net-zero as soon as viable in the second half of the century.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Similarly, the updated NDC reiterates that Singapore intends to peak emissions at 65 million tonnes of carbon dioxide emission around 2030, and only reach net-zero emissions “as soon as viable” in the second half of the century.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While we now have an absolute emissions target, this absolute figure of 65 MtCO2e is actually equivalent to the 36% reduction in Emissions Intensity from 2005 levels by 2030 and, hence, it is the exact same target that was set back in 2015.

sections.label: Singapore electricity generation sources
sections.summary: As at July 2020, 96% of Singapore's electricity came from natural gas, 1.2% from coal and petroleum products, and 2.8% from other sources including solar.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: According to statistics from Singapore’s Energy Market Authority, as at July 2020, 96% of our electricity in Singapore is produced from natural gas, 1.2% is from coal and petroleum products and 2.8% is from other sources, including solar.

sections.label: Oil firms cutting jobs
sections.summary: BP, ExxonMobil and Shell announced job cuts, with Shell targeting 500 job cuts at Pulau Bukom by 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In June 2020, BP announced it is cutting 10,000 jobs or 15% of its workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In October 2020, ExxonMobil announced it is cutting 14,000 jobs globally, 15% of its workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Closer to home, Shell is targeting to cut 500 jobs by 2023 at Pulau Bukom from the current 1,300 staff today, and with refining capacity halved in the next one to two years.

sections.label: Industrial emissions share in 2017
sections.summary: In 2017, about 75% of Singapore's industrial emissions came from this sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In 2017, about 75% of our industrial emissions were from this sector.

sections.label: Call to fight climate change
sections.summary: The speaker urges the nation to set higher goals and be more courageous against climate change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As a nation, let us challenge ourselves to push the boundaries further to not be afraid to set the bar higher for the sake of our children and to be more courageous in our collective fight against the existential threat of climate change.

sections.label: Carbon tax level inadequate
sections.summary: The speaker says the current carbon tax level is far too low and the $10 to $15 level is inadequate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: I think for the first question on the cabon tax, as mentioned by Member Louis Ng as well, the current carbon tax level is far too low and I would not want to pre-empt my colleague who will be speaking on this further.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: But I would say that, at this point in time, if you look at the Government's plan to review the tax rate by 2023, I think the $10 to $15 level is a level we believe – and I believe that Member Louis Ng has also agreed that it is inadequate.

sections.label: Energy constraints and solar target
sections.summary: The speaker notes geographical constraints, a 2 GWp solar target by 2030, and possible solar imports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: So, again, if we just use our energy sources, I do recognise that we have geographical constraints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: And even in the use of solar energy, for example, we have set a target to reach 2 GWps by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: I think in the last sitting in January, some of the Members have also asked about this question.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: I also understand that certain projects are basically in the pipeline in terms of potentially importing solar energy from our neighbours, or even from Australia, in terms of the project that is on-going there.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: I believe there are various technological pathways through which we can achieve some of these targets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: But this is where, in the first place, for us to be able to recognise this climate emergency and to basically set ourselves a bit more of an ambitious target, given that Singapore has always had this history of outperforming its original expectations.

sections.label: Climate effects in Singapore
sections.summary: Singapore has felt climate change effects such as warming temperatures and increased rainfall causing ponding.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Here, in our island city state, we have felt the effects of climate change first-hand, such as warming temperatures, and increased levels in annual rainfall have caused ponding during the monsoon seasons, with the rains last month making it the wettest January we have had in 30 years.

sections.label: Sustainability sector job creation
sections.summary: The Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment announced over 50,000 new and upgraded jobs will be created in the sector in the next 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: With the Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment's announcement that more than 50,000 new and upgraded jobs will be created in the next 10 years for the sector.

sections.label: Singapore climate change perceptions poll
sections.summary: A December 2019 poll found over 90% aware of climate change, almost 80% prepared to act, but less than half knew what to do.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In December 2019, a poll on climate change perceptions by the National Climate Change Secretariat in Singapore revealed that over 90% of those polled were aware of climate change and its impact, and almost 80% were prepared to play their part towards a low-carbon Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, less than half of those polled said they knew what they could do to address it.

sections.label: Generation Z sustainable brand spending
sections.summary: A US Forbes 2019 report found 62% of Generation Z in the workforce prefer sustainable brands, and over half would spend more on them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: A US Forbes 2019 report found that 62% of Generation Z, who were already in the workforce, prefer to buy from sustainable brands, and more than half of them stated that they were willing to spend more on such products.

sections.label: Mangroves, seagrass carbon storage, Sultan Shoal
sections.summary: Research shows mangroves and seagrass store more carbon than other forests, and the Sultan Shoal project considered science, conservation, biodiversity and development together.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Research has shown that mangroves can store three to five times more carbon per hectare than other forest types, and sea grass meadows are up to 35 times better than rainforests at storing carbon.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Sultan Shoal project in connection with the development at Tuas which commenced in 2013 was an example where an environmental impact study was done, public volunteers were engaged, and science, conservation, biodiversity and development needs were carefully considered together.

sections.label: Urging Government to act on climate
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to accelerate and build on existing efforts in consultation with all stakeholders before it is too late.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: When we talk about climate change, the conversation often begins with us thinking about what kind of world we want to leave for our children and grandchildren.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: But in order to secure this, the time to act is now, and I urge the Government to accelerate and continue building on the good efforts which are in place in consultation with all stakeholders before it is too late.

sections.label: Woodgrove residents recycling and repair suggestions
sections.summary: Woodgrove residents suggested more active recycling points with partners like Tzu Chi Singapore and a repair centre in Residents Committee Centres with Repair Kopitiam.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Suggestions by other Woodgrove residents also included, one, setting up more active recycling points within our community, partnering with Northwest CDCs and organisations such as Tzu Chi Singapore where eco-awareness and proper recycling tips can be shared with our residents; two, setting up a repair centre in the Residents Committee Centres, working with partners such as Repair Kopitiam.

sections.label: Woodgrove sustainability app and initiatives
sections.summary: Woodgrove will collaborate with SIBL, apply for SGEcoFund for a Go-Green app, and hold workshops and community initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: As this may prove to be helpful in terms of promoting sustainable living, Woodgrove will be collaborating with Singapore Institute of Building Limited (SIBL), and applying for the SGEcoFund to explore the possibility of developing such an app, where residents can interact and pick up Green Advocate skills virtually.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We also intend to explore ways to incorporate features such as a carbon footprint calculator, which would enable residents to key in and measure relevant data points including their utilities consumption, mode of transportation and time taken in commutes, food consumption and sources of production, and the number of items and weightage of items which they have recycled.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: If successful, this Go-Green app will raise greater awareness on environmental  issues  related  to  waste,  water  and  energy,  while encouraging the community to collectively shift to an eco-friendly lifestyle through app-based education and gamification.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Tapping on the expertise of SIBL and other climate change VWOs and NGOs, more in-person workshops will also be taking place in the Community Centres, Residents' Committee and even the private estates in Woodgrove, allowing our residents access to more hands-on learning experiences through events such as active recycling and upcycling of old abandoned items and the exchange of pre-loved items in flea markets.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In summary, I would use the alphabets, A, B and C to describe the on-going and upcoming initiatives which Woodgrove will be implementing in playing our part against climate change as a Community.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We are stepping up on the actions which will be introduced in our community, such as building more community gardens, setting up more active recycling points and training more Green Advocates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Exploring and trying out new methods to increase sustainability awareness.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This will include creating a mobile application as what I have shared earlier with the House and encouraging residents to start embracing not just the existing 3Rs, but an additional 2Rs: "refuse" and "repair" as well.

sections.label: Community infrastructure and mobile apps
sections.summary: Woodgrove will build more community gardens and recycling stations and design mobile apps to educate residents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We will step up building community infrastructures to deal with climate change such as more community gardens and recycling stations and encourage active participation from our residents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We will be boldly trying out projects that have not been implemented before, including designing mobile apps to educate more residents on how to do their part to protect the environment, such as refusing to use environmentally damaging items and trying to repair old items as far as possible to reduce wastage.

sections.label: Singapore population growth 2000 to 2019
sections.summary: Singapore's population grew from 4 million in 2000 to 5.7 million in 2019, a 41% increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Our population grew from 4 million in the year 2000 to 5.7 million in 2019, an increase of 41% over 20 years.

sections.label: Citizenships, residencies and population projections
sections.summary: Singapore awards about 25,000 citizenships and 30,000 permanent residencies yearly, reaching 6 million by 2030 and 10 million by 2095.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: While the Government has reduced immigration growth somewhat since 2011 and promises that it has no population target to achieve, it has continued to award about 25,000 new citizenships and 30,000 permanent residencies every year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: At that rate, we will still reach 6 million people by 2030, and 10 million in 2095!

sections.label: Holding population constant at 5.7 million
sections.summary: Holding population constant at 5.7 million would ease housing pressure and avoid cutting forests for land supply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If we choose to hold our population constant at around 5.7 million by only awarding enough new citizenships to maintain but not increase our current population, the pressure on providing more housing will ease immediately and there is no need to cut down more forests to increase land supply.

sections.label: Singapore climate commitments compared internationally
sections.summary: Singapore's Paris Agreement commitments allow net emissions increase to 2030, unlike European countries and China's 2060 carbon neutrality goal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Looking at the bigger picture, our climate mitigation commitments under the Paris Climate Agreement fall far short in comparison to many other countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Singapore's climate commitments allow for a net increase of emissions up to 2030, and merely promise a slight reduction from a hypothetically projected "business-as-usual" benchmark.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: On the other hand, many European countries have committed to a net decrease in emissions, and even China has committed to achieve carbon neutrality by 2060.

sections.label: Ulu Pandan forest cutting pause
sections.summary: The speaker supports preserving forests and proposes halting the cutting of Ulu Pandan forest until the post-COVID development roadmap is clear.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We express our support of the preservation of our forests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We propose that the cutting down of the Ulu Pandan forest should be put on hold immediately until we are clear what our post-COVID development roadmap will be.

sections.label: Greenery coverage mostly man-made
sections.summary: The speaker states that although greenery coverage is about 47%, much of the greenery is man-made.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Regarding the first question, even though our greenery coverage is about 47%, much of the greenery is man-made.

sections.label: 10 million population projection
sections.summary: The speaker says the 10 million figure is a projection based on population growth rate, not a figure read in a report.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: On the second question regarding the 10 million figure, this is a projection based on the growth rate of our population, not a figure that I have read in some report.

sections.label: BTO market and HDB policies
sections.summary: The speaker thanks Mr Don Wee and says the tight BTO market is not due to slow tree cutting, suggesting HDB could tweak policies and step up flat building.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):    I thank Member Mr Don Wee for the question.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: I think the tight situation of the BTO market is not a result of not cutting down trees fast enough.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Because the HDB could tweak its policies in various aspects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Now demand for BTO flats has increased, perhaps HDB could step up the building of these flats.

sections.label: Global warming and G20 stimulus
sections.summary: The speaker states the world is 1.2 degrees Celsius hotter than before the Industrial Revolution, projects a three-degree rise by century's end, and notes Mr Guterres said G20 nations spent 50% more stimulus on fossil fuels than low carbon energy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The world is 1.2-degrees Celsius hotter than it was before the Industrial Revolution and if current trends continue, global temperatures will rise by three-degrees Celsius by the end of this century.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Mr Guterres noted that the G20 Nations has spent 50% more of their respective stimulus packages on fossil fuel production and consumption than on low carbon energy.

sections.label: Transport electrification by 2040
sections.summary: The Government is aiming to fully electrify transport by 2040.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government is aiming to fully electrify transport by 2040.

sections.label: Shell Singapore job and capacity cuts
sections.summary: Shell's shift to low-carbon fuels will cost Singapore 500 jobs and half of Pulau Bukom's processing capacity in three years, while ExxonMobil, BP and Chevron cut global workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Royal Dutch Shell pivoted away from crude oil towards a low-carbon slate of fuels will cost Singapore 500 jobs and half of the processing capacity in Pulau Bukom in the next three years; while ExxonMobil, BP and Chevron will be cutting the global workforce as well.

sections.label: ACRA simplified sustainability reporting proposal
sections.summary: ACRA could consider requiring simplified environmental sustainability reporting for private limited companies with revenue over 100 million dollars and more than 200 employees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: ACRA could consider requiring simplified environmental sustainability reporting for private limited companies with the revenue of over 100 million dollars and with more than 200 employees.

sections.label: Energy efficiency in power industry
sections.summary: The Energy Conservation Act of 2013 is in place, and the power industry produces 39.7% of Singapore's greenhouse gas emissions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Much has already been put in place by way of the Energy Conservation Act of 2013.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I would now like to talk specifically about energy efficiency in the power industry, which produces 39.7% of greenhouse gas emissions in Singapore.

sections.label: Thermal efficiency gains cut emissions
sections.summary: A 4 percentage-point improvement in power plant thermal efficiency cuts 1.65 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent, about 5% of Singapore's 2050 target, and saves almost $100 million yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, a 4 percentage-point improvement in thermal efficiency of power plants will reduce carbon dioxide emissions by 1.65 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent, or about 5% of Singapore's 2050 carbon dioxide reduction target.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It will also save almost $100 million a year in natural gas costs at current prices.

sections.label: Call for climate emergency declaration
sections.summary: Given the urgency of the climate situation, the speaker calls for the House to acknowledge a state of climate emergency in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Given the urgency of the climate situation, I call for the House to acknowledge that a state of climate emergency exists in Singapore.

sections.label: Paris Agreement and science-based targets
sections.summary: Singapore committed to the Paris Climate Agreement, may have three decades or less to reach net zero, and can set more ambitious science-based targets for three key outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore, along with nearly 200 other countries, has committed to the Paris Climate Agreement and its goal of limiting global warming to below two degrees Celsius, compared to pre-industrial levels.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to scientists on the United Nation's Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, we may have only three decades or less to drawdown our emissions to net zero, for us to achieve the Paris Climate Goal.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In terms of climate change mitigation, Singapore can do our part by setting more ambitious science-based targets for three key outcomes.

sections.label: Emerging Stronger Taskforce partnership
sections.summary: The Emerging Stronger Taskforce, co-chaired by Minister Desmond Lee and Mr Tan Chong Meng, is an example of Government-corporate partnership.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Emerging Stronger Taskforce, co-chaired by Minister Desmond Lee and Mr Tan Chong Meng, is an example of a much-needed Government-corporate partnership.

sections.label: Youth pride and climate leadership
sections.summary: The speaker recalls pride as a young Singaporean and says youths are ready to be prouder if Singapore shows global leadership on causes like climate change.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And I remember the immense pride I felt as a very young Singaporean.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I think our youths today are ready to be even prouder of Singapore, especially if Singapore takes seriously and demonstrates global leadership in the many causes that our youths care deeply and passionately about, including climate change.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Of course, climate change is a problem much bigger than Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Prof Koh Lian Pin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But tackling this problem is also an opportunity for us to be part of something much bigger than ourselves, and be proud of it.

sections.label: Emissions by sector
sections.summary: At the primary level, 40% of emissions come from power-generation, 40% from industry and 15% from transportation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Broadly speaking, at the primary level, 40% of our emissions today comes from power-generation, 40% from industry and 15% are from transportation.

sections.label: Natural gas efficiency and energy imports
sections.summary: Industry experts say new natural gas power plants can yield 4%-5% efficiency gains, far less than the 50% target, and Singapore must rely on low-carbon electricity or energy imports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: The industry experts I speak to inform me that even the new natural gas power plants can yield a 4%-5% efficiency gains, far less than the 50% target.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: But I doubt Singaporeans will be comfortable with that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: And given our lack of renewable energy locally because of our intermittent sunlight, we must rely on imports which means either import direct low-carbon electricity imports or low-carbon energy imports like hydrogen.

sections.label: Electricity as scarce growth constraint
sections.summary: There will be a crunch in low-carbon electricity immediately after 2030 until technology matures, so electricity must be treated as a scarce growth constraint.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: As explained earlier, there will be a crunch in low-carbon electricity immediately after 2030, until technology matures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Therefore, when we grow our industries, we must start treating electricity as a scarce growth constraint, much as we treat foreign manpower today.

sections.label: Carbon price trending to international norms
sections.summary: The speaker is cautious about increasing carbon tax during the COVID-19 pandemic but says the carbon price must over time trend towards international norms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: While I am cautious about increasing carbon tax amidst the COVID-19 pandemic, it is clear to me that over time, our carbon price must trend towards the international norms.

sections.label: Black Rock and Microsoft climate
sections.summary: Black Rock asks companies to disclose net-zero plans, and Microsoft wants carbon neutrality by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Black Rock, which controls $9 trillion assets, is asking all companies to disclose a plan for how their business model will be compatible with a net-zero economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Microsoft wants to be carbon neutral by 2030.

sections.label: MAS environmental risk guidelines
sections.summary: MAS announced Environment Risk Management Guidelines, and the speaker hopes MAS and MFA push financial institutions on disclosure, training, coal financing and global climate rules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: MAS recently announced Environment Risk Management Guidelines is a step in the right direction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: I hope MAS can actively get our FIs to disclose more to the public and encourage them to conduct environmental risk training programs for senior management and board members, and persuade our FIs to stop financing of coal power plants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Lastly, MFA can also draw on these expertise to hopefully play a bigger role in shaping the global climate change policies, and push for transparent and effective global rules, including in the area of cap and trade, which could benefit Singapore, should we go big on developing overseas carbon offsets.

sections.label: Singapore carbon tax rate
sections.summary: The carbon tax is $5 per tonne, rising to $10 to $15 by 2030, below the UN IPCC median of $95.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The current rate is set at $5 per metric tonne of greenhouse gas emissions, set to be increased to $10 to $15 dollars a tonne by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This figure falls far below recommended amounts by just about every credible source.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The median estimate called for by the UN Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change is $95.

sections.label: Carbon tax coverage limits
sections.summary: The carbon tax covers only the largest industrial facilities emitting over 2,000 tons of carbon dioxide, about 30 to 40 companies.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Moreover, the exiting carbon tax is limited to just the largest industrial facilities – those emitting in excess of 2,000 tons of carbon dioxide, and effectively covers just about 30 to 40 companies.

sections.label: Electric vehicles and petrochemicals
sections.summary: Electric and hybrid vehicles number about 1,400 and 52,000 out of 950,000, while petrochemicals contribute around $81 billion or 3% of national output.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As another example, the number of hybrid and electric vehicles in Singapore remain tiny: about 1,400 electric vehicles and 52,000 hybrids, out of our 950,000 strong fleet, a mere 6%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The petrochemicals industry currently contributes a nontrivial share to Singapore's national output, around $81 billion or 3%, and our nation is currently the world's seventh largest exporter of chemicals and industry.

sections.label: Carbon price starting point
sections.summary: The speaker says a starting price of around $58 would place Singapore at the midpoint among industrialised economies, and asks how the Government arrived at $15.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While the specific price is certainly up for debate and should, ideally, be deliberated by a panel of experts with representatives from business, environmental civil society groups, policymakers from the NEA and MSE, and academics, a starting point of around $58 would at least place Singapore at the midpoint among industrialised economies, even if it remains below what would be necessary for decisive climate change mitigation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A figure within this range would be a very useful start for the panel and our civil service to deliberate.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And if I may turn the question around, posed by Minister Fu: how did the Government arrive at the $15?

sections.label: Carbon tax position defended
sections.summary: The speaker supports the carbon tax as more credible with preferable distributional outcomes than schemes more attractive on paper.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I attribute it to the shared rarified air that we have all the way up here.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: That said, I have taken this position because I believe that the carbon tax is not only more credible, but it also embeds preferable distributional outcomes, relative to schemes that may be more attractive from an efficiency standpoint on paper, but ultimately fall short in real-world conditions.

sections.label: Singapore positioned for climate action
sections.summary: Singapore's advanced services economy positions it to address climate change, an emergency calling for drastic measures.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Singapore has the fortune of already being a technologically advanced, services-oriented economy, and hence inherently better positioned to embrace more decisive moves toward addressing environmental issues and, in particular, the threat of climate change.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Climate change is an emergency, which calls for drastic measures.

sections.label: Support for amended Motion
sections.summary: The speaker expresses support for the Motion as amended by Hougang MP Mr Dennis Tan.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: With that parting thought, I express my support for the Motion, as amended by the Member of Parliament from Hougang, Mr Dennis Tan.

sections.label: Zero Waste Masterplan
sections.summary: The inaugural Zero Waste Masterplan aims to transform Singapore into a Zero Waste Nation powered by a circular economy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Our inaugural Zero Waste Masterplan strives to transform Singapore into a Zero Waste Nation powered by a circular economy.

sections.label: Ministry renamed for Sustainability
sections.summary: The Government's commitment is underscored by renaming the Ministry to include "Sustainability".

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The Government's commitment is underscored by our decision to rename my Ministry to include "Sustainability".

sections.label: Solar deployment targets
sections.summary: Ambitious solar deployment targets are set at 1.5 giga-watt peak by 2025 and at least 2 giga-watt peak by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, we have set ambitious solar deployment targets of 1.5 giga-watt peak of solar deployment by 2025 and at least 2 giga-watt peak by 2030.

sections.label: Energy & Chemicals sector contribution
sections.summary: The E&C sector contributed around 3% of Singapore's GDP and employed over 25,000 people in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The Energy & Chemicals sector (E&C sector) contributed around 3% of Singapore's GDP and employed over 25,000 people in 2019.

sections.label: Neste plant capacity doubling
sections.summary: Neste opened its plant's first phase in 2010 and will double refining capacity to about 2.6 million tons of renewable fuels yearly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Neste opened the first phase of its plant in 2010 and will be doubling its refining capacity to about 2.6 million tons of renewable fuels per annum.

sections.label: Paris Agreement emissions pledges
sections.summary: Singapore pledged to peak emissions at 65 million tonnes around 2030, halve to 33 million tonnes by 2050, and seek net-zero.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: As a signatory to the Paris Agreement, we have pledged to peak our emissions at 65 million tonnes of CO2-equivalent around 2030, and aspire to halve emissions from its peak to 33 million tonnes by 2050.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We will seek to achieve net-zero emissions as soon as viable in the second half of the century.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: After deliberation, we have made several enhancements to our NDC, including a clear peaking target and detailed implementation efforts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: For example, even if we were to put solar PVs on every single rooftop our our HDB estates, we will still need to rely on natural gas for our electricity needs unless there are breakthroughs in needle-moving technologies like low carbon fuels, such as hydrogen or low carbon solutions like CCUS.

sections.label: Carbon tax coverage
sections.summary: Singapore implemented a carbon tax in 2019, covering 80% of emissions with no exemptions for covered facilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Central to our climate mitigation strategy is our carbon tax.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We are the first in Southeast Asia to have implemented a carbon tax in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: At 80% of our total emissions, our carbon tax coverage is one of the most comprehensive globally and we have not provided exemptions to any of our covered facilities.

sections.label: Supporting low-carbon transition
sections.summary: The carbon tax is not stand-alone; the Government will spend more than collected revenue in the first five years on emissions reductions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Our carbon tax is not a stand-alone measure.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We are committed to supporting our businesses and households transit to a low-carbon future and are prepared to spend more than what we collect in carbon tax revenue in the first five years on worthwhile projects to achieve emissions reductions.

sections.label: Phasing out combustion engine vehicles
sections.summary: The Government aims to phase out internal combustion engine vehicles and have all vehicles on cleaner energy by 2040.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The Government aims to phase out internal combustion engine vehicles and have all vehicles run on cleaner energy by 2040.

sections.label: Singapore Green Plan 2030 launch
sections.summary: The Government is preparing a whole-of-nation Singapore Green Plan 2030, a multi-Ministry effort with sectoral targets.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Over the last few months, the Government has been making preparations to launch a whole-of-nation movement to advance the sustainability agenda in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We call this the Singapore Green Plan 2030 or, in short, the Green Plan.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: This is a multi-Ministry effort and will be a major policy priority for this Government.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Under the Green Plan, agencies will set ambitious and concrete targets on a sectoral basis, building on what we have achieved.

sections.label: Partnering private sector on sustainability
sections.summary: The Government intends to partner the private sector and people to mitigate and adapt to climate change.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The Government has every intent, as the Motion states, to partner the private sector and the people of Singapore, to deepen and accelerate efforts to mitigate and adapt to climate change and to embrace sustainability in the development of Singapore.

sections.label: City ambitions and trade-offs
sections.summary: As a city, Singapore is as ambitious as Beijing, Tokyo and Seoul, involving candid discussions on costs and trade-offs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: On the other hand, as a city, we are as ambitious, if not more so, as Beijing, Tokyo and Seoul.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: This will involve candid discussions on the costs and trade-offs involved, which we will have to bear, whether as consumers, as businesses or as the Government.

sections.label: Trade-offs and future costs
sections.summary: Trade-offs and changes must be pursued because not doing so will inflict greater future costs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Trade-offs we must make and changes we must pursue, for the consequences of not doing so will inflict on us costs that are many times greater in the future.

sections.label: Co-creating sustainable future
sections.summary: Climate change requires envisioning a new future, and Singapore will co-create a sustainable future for present and future generations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Climate change requires us to envision a new future, and be prepared to give up the old to embrace the new.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: And we firmly believe that in Singapore, we will co-create a sustainable future for present and future generations.

sections.label: Acting today for future generations
sections.summary: The Government has accepted trade-offs to current economic growth to safeguard Singapore's long-term well-being, amid unpredictable weather patterns.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: At the price of popular vote, the Government of today has often bitten the bullet, knowing that some benefits will only be reaped by our future generations.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: The trade-offs on current economic growth are real and tangible especially in light of the heavy pandemic that has cost to our economy.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Yet, to safeguard Singapore’s long-term well-being in the ways that even the deepest financial reserves cannot, we must act today.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: We then saw mudslides and flooding in various parts of Singapore and temperatures dipped to a low of 21.1 degrees celsius.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: These unpredictable weather patterns have increased in frequency the last decade in Singapore.

sections.label: Calling for climate emergency declaration
sections.summary: The passage says the hour has come for Singapore to declare a climate emergency, joining over 30 countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The hour has come for Singapore to call a spade a spade and join the close to the over 30 other countries in the world who have declared climate emergencies.

sections.label: Urban heat vulnerability in areas
sections.summary: Cooling Singapore's 2020 study lists Woodlands, Serangoon, Geylang, Sengkang and Punggol as very high vulnerability for urban heat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Extensively built areas like, for example, Woodlands, Serangoon, Geylang, Sengkang and Punggol are listed as very high vulnerability in terms of urban heat, according to Cooling Singapore’s 2020 study.

sections.label: Switzerland carbon tax revenue redistribution
sections.summary: In Switzerland, two thirds of carbon tax revenue is redistributed to households per capita and to firms by payroll.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In Switzerland, two thirds of the collected revenue from their carbon tax is redistributed to households, on a per capita basis, and to firms in proportion to their payroll.

sections.label: Golf club land lease renewals
sections.summary: Seven of eight golf clubs whose leases were due to expire between 2021 and 2023 have had leases renewed to some extent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The land leases of seven of eight golf clubs whose leases were due to expire between 2021 and 2023 have been renewed to some extent.

sections.label: Sustainability reporting incentives for SGX companies
sections.summary: The passage suggests stronger incentives and disincentives for quality sustainability reporting by SGX companies aligned with GRI and TCFD standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On this theme, I have a few suggestions for Government and governance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I suggest a stronger suite of incentives and disincentives for quality sustainability reporting for SGX companies in line with Global Reporting Initiative and Taskforce on Climate-related Financial Disclosures standards, with additional support and a longer transitional runway for small-to-mid cap companies.

sections.label: Tengah forest clearing and undisclosed study
sections.summary: 700 hectares of Tengah forest was cleared, and the HDB has not yet disclosed the environmental baseline study.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, 700 hectares of Tengah forest was cleared.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The environmental baseline study for this has not yet been disclosed by the HDB.

sections.label: Sunseap Charge+ EV charging
sections.summary: Sunseap's Charge+ is one of the first companies involved in EV charging in Singapore and does business across Asia Pacific.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, Sunseap's Charge+ is one of the first companies to get involved in EV charging here and the company does business across the Asia Pacific.

sections.label: URA Masterplan 2019 forest sites
sections.summary: The URA's Masterplan 2019 lists 20 forest sites as slated for development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The URA's Masterplan 2019 lists 20 forest sites as being slated for development.

sections.label: Reviewing KPIs for green goals
sections.summary: There is room to review KPIs applied to Ministries and Statutory Boards to incorporate green goals and targets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Lastly, Sir, on the theme of a national green agenda, let me talk about indicators of national development and welfare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There is room for us to review the KPIs applied to Ministries and Statutory Boards to incorporate green goals and targets, such as reducing net carbon emissions alongside reflecting more transparency in reporting these.

sections.label: New Zealand public sector carbon neutral
sections.summary: One of New Zealand's commitments for its public sector is to be carbon neutral by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One of New Zealand's commitments for its public sector is to be carbon neutral by 2025.

sections.label: Singapore emissions peak 2030
sections.summary: Singapore aims to peak emissions in 2030 while the IPCC recommends 45% reduction from 2010 levels by 2030 and net-zero by 2050.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Singapore aims to peak emissions in 2030 while the IPCC recommends 45% emissions reduction from 2010 levels by 2030 and net-zero by 2050.

sections.label: Singapore carbon tax comprehensive
sections.summary: The carbon tax in Singapore is one of the most comprehensive in the world.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: In fact, the carbon tax in Singapore is one of the most comprehensive in the world.

sections.label: Carbon tax coverage of emissions
sections.summary: Applying the carbon tax to key nodes covers 80% of Singapore's emissions, with transport fuel emissions making coverage higher than 80%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: By selecting these key nodes and applying the carbon tax there, for example, the power companies and the key emitters in industry, we have been able to cover 80% of emissions in Singapore, and this is an extremely effective way of doing so.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The remaining 20%: the highest proportion of the remainder actually comes from transport fuel emissions, which are already fairly substantially taxed in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: So, our coverage is even higher than 80% when one talks about the carbon tax coverage.

sections.label: Singapore carbon tax rate and facilities
sections.summary: Singapore's $5 per tonne carbon tax applies to facilities emitting over 25,000 tonnes annually, with a planned rise to $10-$15 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Currently, Singapore's carbon tax of $5 per tonne of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions is levied only on key facilities as mentioned by Senior Minister Teo whose annual emissions are more than 25,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Government aims to raise the tax to between $10 and $15 by 2030, subject to a review in 2023.

sections.label: Suggested carbon tax increase timeline
sections.summary: The speaker suggests raising the carbon tax gradually to $30-$55 by 2030, $50-$90 by 2035 and $75-$120 by 2040.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I am hopeful that we will emerge from the COVID-19 crisis by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Therefore, I suggest that we increase our carbon tax gradually, so that we will be able meet higher targets incrementally, based on the following timeline and quantums: between $30 and $55 by 2030; between $50 and $90 by 2035; and between $75 and $120 by 2040.

sections.label: MAS Green Loan Grant Scheme
sections.summary: MAS introduced the Green and Sustainability-linked Loan Grant Scheme last November, effective 1 January 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Last November, MAS introduced the Green and Sustainability-linked Loan Grant Scheme (GSLS) which will come into effect on 1 January 2021.

sections.label: Singapore warming and emissions targets
sections.summary: Singapore is almost one degree Celsius hotter than the 1950s, ranks in the top 30 for per capita carbon emissions, and targets peaking at 65 million tonnes by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: Singapore is now almost one degree Celsius hotter than our pre-industrial 1950s and heating up twice as fast as the rest of the world.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: Today, Singapore remains in the top 30 nations in carbon emissions per capita out of 142, standing at 8.45 tonnes per capita.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: For this reason and as party to the Paris Climate Agreement, we have set a target to peak at 65 million tonnes of carbon dioxide by 2030, a target I urge this House to review.

sections.label: Older trees sequester more carbon
sections.summary: A 2015 Singapore study shows older trees sequester significantly more carbon than younger trees planted in new parks or sidewalks.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: A 2015 study with Singapore shows that older trees sequester a significantly larger amount of carbon than younger trees we plant in new parks or sidewalks.

sections.label: Forests and golf course land
sections.summary: Clementi Forest covers 85 hectares and Ulu Pandan Forest 33 hectares, and the speaker suggests using golf course land before forest land.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: On our forests: the Clementi Forest covers 85 hectares and Ulu Pandan Forest, 33 hectares.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: It would be ecologically responsible of us to consider utilising portions of the 1,500 hectares across 17 golf courses, before reaching into our forest land.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: I am encouraged to hear from Minister Desmond Lee earlier today that by 2030, 400 hectares of golf course land will be taken back for redevelopment.

sections.label: Singapore green space per capita
sections.summary: Singapore aims to raise green space per capita to eight square metres by 2030, below WHO's nine square metres.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: Singapore has set a goal to raise our green space per capita to eight square metres by 2030, just shy of the WHO's recommended minimum of nine square metres per capita, and far from the ideal 50 square metres.

sections.label: Lower carbon targets, preserve forests
sections.summary: The speaker proposes lowering Singapore's 2030 carbon targets and re-zoning Clementi and Ulu Pandan Forests as nature reserves.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: In summary, for the purpose of mitigating Singapore's carbon emissions, I propose that Singapore further lower our 2030 targets for carbon emissions, not only by deployment of technology, but also by preserving the forests we have, especially re-zoning Clementi and Ulu Pandan Forests as nature reserves while exploring other land space for our housing and industrial needs.

sections.label: Public EV charging points
sections.summary: The Government plans 28,000 public charging points and seeks private sector help for electric vehicle infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Government is already planning to install 28,000 public charging points and is looking to work with the private sector to ramp up the infrastructure for electric vehicles.

sections.label: Condo EV charging rules
sections.summary: With over 16% of Singaporeans in condominiums, the speaker urges regulations and incentives for condo EV charging infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As over 16% of Singaporeans live in condominiums, I urge the Government to introduce regulations and incentives for condos to provide EV charging infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For a start, new condos should be required to set aside a certain number of their parking spaces as charging points.

sections.label: Industry data-sharing mechanisms
sections.summary: The Government can set up data-sharing mechanisms within and across industries, particularly for key industrial sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Government can step in by setting up data-sharing mechanisms within and across industries, particularly for key industrial sectors.

sections.label: EV adoption and battery swapping
sections.summary: EV adoption lags because buyers worry about higher costs and range anxiety, and battery swapping could address charging time concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: EVs have not been adopted as quickly as we hope because potential buyers are wary of their higher costs and suffer from range anxiety – the worry that their EVs will run out of electricity before they can reach charging points.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Imagine if one could just drive into an energy station and swap the car battery, similar to the option for many mobile phones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This would address the concerns over the time needed to charge the EVs, unlike the quick petroleum top up we can get for internal combustion engine vehicles.

sections.label: Copies and Singapore emissions share
sections.summary: Copies were given to the Clerk for distribution, and Singapore makes up 0.1% of global emissions annually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Do you have copies made for all the Members?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: I have given copies to the Clerk for distribution.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: Today, Singapore makes up 0.1% of global emissions annually.

sections.label: Climate change motion amendment
sections.summary: The proposed amendment acknowledges climate change as a global emergency and calls on Government, private sector, civil society and people to deepen mitigation and adaptation efforts.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: In the spirit of mutual improvement towards the same goal, I hope both sides of the House will support the amendment.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: This is what the proposed amendments to the Motion reads: "That this House acknowledges that climate change is a global emergency and threat to mankind and calls on the Government in partnership with the private sector, civil society and the people of Singapore to deepen and accelerate efforts to mitigate and adapt to climate change and to embrace sustainability in the development of Singapore." Mr Speaker, the decarbonisation journey is a multi-faceted and dynamic one.

sections.label: Annual ESG Report requirement
sections.summary: Companies must publish an annual ESG Report based on standardised reporting frameworks.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: One, companies must publish an annual ESG Report based on standardised reporting frameworks.

sections.label: MAS list of reporting frameworks
sections.summary: MAS is to provide a list of reporting frameworks that can be mandated for annual ESG reporting.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: Two, MAS to provide a list of reporting frameworks that can be mandated for the annual ESG reporting.

sections.label: Mandating frameworks for larger companies
sections.summary: Mandating specific reporting frameworks should begin with larger public listed and multinational companies, with support and induction for SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
