sentences.text: I am certainly cognisant that it will be tall order for many companies without the ability to administer and comply with a reporting framework.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: Hence, the suggestion is to begin mandating specific framework of reporting from the larger public listed companies, including the multinational companies.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: The larger companies in Singapore can take the lead in adopting the frameworks so at the start, the support will be given to provided induction for SMEs who may have limited knowledge about their supply chains or their production footprint.

sections.label: Green jobs and sustainability skills
sections.summary: Proposes working with industries and the public sector on green jobs, skills and professionalising the green economy, possibly via an ITM pillar.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: Three, work with industries and public sector to outline types of future green jobs and constantly align on skills and competencies that are required for such roles in emerging sectors Four, develop understanding of sustainability as a career and professionalising the Green Economy as the current perception is that green jobs usually exist in non-profit organisations.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: We can be accelerated at the beginning of this transformation through adding a pillar in the Industry Transformation Map (ITM) with specific focus on sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: Over time, the sustainability element can then be incorporated directly under each of the 23 ITMs.

sections.label: Amendment on climate emergency wording
sections.summary: A sub-amendment proposes replacing "a climate emergency" with "that climate change is a global emergency and a threat to mankind".

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: All hands on deck, let us navigate this adventure together!

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: It has been proposed as a sub-amendment that after the word "acknowledges" in Mr Tan's first amendment, to leave out the words "a climate emergency" and there to insert the words "that climate change is a global emergency and a threat to mankind".

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The Question is, "That the words proposed to be left out, be there left out.”

sections.label: Emissions and Paris Agreement targets
sections.summary: Greenhouse gas emissions hit a new high in 2019, and instead of the Paris Agreement's 1.5-degree cap, a three-degree change is on track.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Greenhouse gas emissions reached a new high in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: The Paris Agreement aimed to cap this century’s temperature increase at 1.5-degree Celsius.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: But instead we are on track for three-degree Celsius change.

sections.label: NTU E-mobility emissions reduction
sections.summary: An NTU Energy Research Institute roadmap found EVs are expected to cut Singapore emissions by up to 64% by 2050.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: The E-mobility Technology Roadmap published by the Energy Research Institute at NTU looked at the data and found that by 2050, EVs are expected to reduce emissions by up to 64% in Singapore.

sections.label: Including civil society in Motion
sections.summary: The speaker supports including the words "civil society" in the Motion's statement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Having said that, I support the inclusion of the word "civil society" into the Motion's statement.

sections.label: Drafting focus on climate action
sections.summary: The draft focuses on actions to deepen and accelerate climate mitigation and adaptation, and the speaker accepts the amendments' rationale.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: We have drafted it that way to focus on actions and how we can deepen and accelerate efforts to mitigate and adapt to climate change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: That was my preference but I recognise the merits of the proposed amendments and I agree with the rationale.

sections.label: Singapore sustainability whole-of-nation movement
sections.summary: Sustainability is part of Singapore's DNA, and the plan is a multi-Ministry effort and a major policy priority for this Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Indeed, sustainability has and always will be a part of Singapore’s DNA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: This whole-of-nation movement to advance the sustainability agenda in Singapore is an important one and I am glad that the plan is a multi-Ministry effort, and that it will be a major policy priority for this Government.

sections.label: Sustainability in national development
sections.summary: Sustainability must become a core part of the nation's development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Sustainability must become a core part of our nation’s development.

sections.label: Amendments to climate motion
sections.summary: Cheryl Chan's amendment was agreed to, and the original Motion as amended is now before the House.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Miss Cheryl Chan's amendment to the original first amendment by Mr Dennis Tan has been agreed to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: We come now to the original amendment, as amended, which is after the words “That this House” to insert the words “acknowledges that climate change is a global emergency and a threat to mankind and”.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The second amendment is in line 2, after the words “private sector” and insert a comma and the words “civil society”.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The original Motion, as amended, is now before the House.
